name: Soulside
label: Dischord
lede: They started on a split single with Dave Grohl's first band, snuck into East Berlin without their guitars, broke up in Holland, and came back twenty-five years later still arguing about what a punk song is for.

eras.title: Lunchmeat, with Dave Grohl on the other side
eras.text: Soulside began as a high school band with a joke name, Lunchmeat, sharing vinyl with Mission Impossible, whose drummer Dave Grohl would end up the most famous person to come out of D.C. punk. By 1986 they'd picked a name they meant: Soulside.

years.h: Four high schoolers start Lunchmeat, later Soulside
years.p: [[Bobby Sullivan|8f4bfc0f-bed1-4cb8-8b95-9fe2a7c9ffd2]] sings, [[Scott McCloud|11e1e118-8744-45f0-9c37-dc4944541134]] plays guitar, [[Alexis Fleisig|e99216da-6570-4906-89c2-aa3622cf2174]] drums and [[Chris Thomson|e79601f0-2aa6-415c-886e-570aea8acea1]] plays bass in Lunchmeat, the band that becomes Soulside.

years.h: Lunchmeat's first record: a split with Mission Impossible
years.p: Lunchmeat share a 7" on Sammich with Mission Impossible, the band [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] drummed in before [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] and Nirvana.

years.h: Lunchmeat becomes Soulside
years.p: Lunchmeat rename themselves Soulside in summer 1986, per Wikipedia. The new name fit a band getting more serious about what it was saying.

eras.title: The MacKaye years
eras.text: Soulside grew up fast in the post-Revolution Summer scene, with Ian MacKaye producing and a rhythm section that could swing. Johnny Temple's arrival on bass set the lineup that would make every record that mattered.

years.h: Soulside's first LP, Less Deep Inside Keeps
years.p: Soulside's debut album, released on Sammich with Dischord behind it, gets the band on the road.

years.h: [[Johnny Temple|d664d24a-618a-45b2-ba5e-c5c8b8e343cb]] replaces Chris Thomson on bass
years.p: Chris Thomson leaves Soulside; he'd later front [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]]. Johnny Temple joins, and the line-up is locked.

years.h: Trigger · Dischord No. 29
years.p: Soulside's eight-song album, cut at Inner Ear with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing, and the band's first record with a Dischord catalog number on the spine.

years.h: Live at DC Space, June 7, 1988

eras.title: Three months, both sides of the Wall
eras.text: In their last year Soulside went further than almost any D.C. band of the era, playing Poland and sneaking into an East German punk show months before the Wall fell. They made their best record, Hot Bodi-Gram, at the end of the tour and broke up before it came out.

years.h: Soulside's Bass 7" · Dischord No. 34
years.p: Soulside release Bass backed with 103 on Dischord before heading to Europe.

q: We couldn't bring guitars nor say we were playing.
years.h: Soulside play an illegal church-basement show in East Berlin
years.p: On a three-month DIY tour of Europe, Poland included, Soulside play one of East Berlin's illegal punk shows in Lutheran churches, the only American band to do so, per Wikipedia and Bobby Sullivan.
years.xp:
Getting in meant crossing at Checkpoint Charlie with no instruments and no admitting there was a gig at all. Dischord's own history singles out the Poland and East Berlin shows as what set the band apart.

The Wall came down that November. By then Soulside was already over.

years.h: Soulside's Hot Bodi-Gram, recorded in Holland
years.p: Soulside cut twelve songs at Tango Studios at the end of their 1989 European tour, with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] producing. One is titled A Love Supreme.

years.h: Soulside split over Bobby Sullivan's lyrics and the music
years.p: Soulside break up right after their 1989 European tour. Wikipedia cites conflict over musical direction and lyrics.
years.xp:
No Echo puts it more pointedly: friction between Bobby Sullivan's politically charged lyrics and what Scott McCloud, Johnny Temple and Alexis Fleisig wanted from the band. Asheville Stages calls it artistic differences.

It split cleanly down the middle. McCloud, Temple and Fleisig, plus producer Eli Janney, would be Girls Against Boys within a year. Sullivan went his own way, into music and organizing.

years.h: Live in Poland, 1989

eras.title: Girls Against Boys, and other exits
eras.text: The breakup produced one of the defining bands of the 1990s underground and scattered the rest into activism, reggae and Circus Lupus. Dischord kept the catalog alive on a single CD.

years.h: Soulside's Soon Come Happy gathers the Dischord records
years.p: Dischord No. 51 puts Soulside's Trigger, the Bass 7" and Hot Bodi-Gram on one Maxi CD.

years.h: [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]] is born
years.p: Soulside's Scott McCloud, Johnny Temple and Alexis Fleisig team up with producer Eli Janney. Temple would also go on to found Akashic Books in Brooklyn.

years.h: Bobby Sullivan takes the other road
years.p: Soulside singer Bobby Sullivan forms 7 League Boots in Boston, mixing reggae and rock, works five years with Food Not Bombs in D.C. and Boston, and helps start D.C.'s Anarchist Black Cross chapter.

eras.title: Twenty-five years later, a new record
eras.text: A documentary premiere pulled the four back into a room, and it didn't stop there. Scattered across continents, they wrote through the pandemic and made their first album in thirty-three years.

years.h: Soulside reunite for the Salad Days premiere
years.p: Soulside reunites to play the premiere of Salad Days: A Decade of Punk in Washington, DC (1980–90). Dischord marks 2014 as the reformation.

years.h: Soulside play Prague for Scott McCloud's 50th
years.p: Soulside play one show in Prague for guitarist Scott McCloud's 50th birthday. European dates follow in 2019.

years.h: Bobby Sullivan writes Revolutionary Threads
years.p: Soulside singer Bobby Sullivan publishes Revolutionary Threads: Rastafari, Social Justice and Cooperative Economics. Now in Asheville, he runs the French Broad Food Co-op.

years.h: Soulside's This Ship 7" · Dischord No. 191
years.p: Soulside's first new music in over thirty years: This Ship backed with Madeleine Said.

years.h: A Brief Moment In The Sun · Dischord No. 192
years.p: Soulside's first album since 1989, written remotely in the pandemic and recorded by [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] at his Magpie Cage studio in Baltimore, with Ian MacKaye pitching in.
play: A Brief Moment In The Sun
